text:
katie: Quick RFC follow-up re: fair queue handoff + abuse autotune. TL;DR: I think we should move per-tenant burst tokens out of the edge gateway into the Quota Service (QSvc) and have the runtime do a soft-degrade based on a fast local cache. Questions: where's the clean interface boundary, how do we keep latency predictable, and how do we enable safe rollbacks?

sam: +1 on moving authoritative state to QSvc. main worry is sync latency on cold/miss paths — we need a fast path in the gateway that handles the 99th percentile without a roundtrip. maybe a short-lived token lease cache (100-500ms) with background refresh.

miguel: agree with sam. we can do a hybrid: gateway checks a local token-bucket replica; if below threshold, call QSvc to acquire/charge. QSvc is the single source for counters and global backpressure policy. gateway fast-path uses allowance from local bucket.

anya: multi-region question: what if gateway and QSvc are in different regions? do we do region-local QSvc instances with eventual convergence? we should avoid cross-region sync on hot paths.

miguel: region-local QSvc instances + deterministic routing for sticky customers. we can shard orgs by org_id % N to pick a primary region. fallback to nearest replica for reads, but writes are routed to primary (async replication). tradeoff: consistency vs local latency.

katie: that sounds reasonable. need to document the tradeoffs: strong consistency for billing/abuse decisions vs eventual for throttling. For abuse prevention, we can tolerate slightly stale info if the runtime applies soft-degrade first (queue/drop) and escalates to hard-block only after QSvc confirms.

devon: quick config example for a token lease that QSvc returns to gateway:
```
{
  "tenant": "org-123",
  "lease_expires_at": 1670000000,
  "tokens": 120,
  "burst_window_ms": 1000,
  "policy": "soft_degrade"
}
```
gateway applies local token decrement; if a request would go negative, gateway calls QSvc `acquire(tenant, n)` which either grants more tokens or returns `overlimit`.

sam: metrics we need: local cache hit ratio, acquire latency P50/P95, QSvc errors by org, resulting 429 vs queueing rate. Also track model-level downstream latencies because our policies may differ for long-running vs short responses.

katie: on abuse autotune: propose per-tenant score that aggregates abnormality signals (rate spike, high failure rate, repeated short completions, invalid inputs). QSvc exposes `score` and `confidence`. Runtime can apply graduated actions: warn -> soft-degrade -> hard limit -> suspend. autotune rules should be bounded and require human review for suspension.

miguel: lightweight classifier idea: features = recent token/sec z-score, 5xx ratio, IP entropy, api_key_age. We can run it in the QSvc protection tier (fast path), store scores as time-decayed counters. heavier ML model runs offline and feeds the thresholds.

anya: enterprise reserved capacity concern: reserved pools should bypass some soft-degrades but not hard abuse actions. need hierarchical quotas: reserved_limit > org_quota > route_quota. QSvc should evaluate the hierarchy and return effective allowance + reason codes.

katie: agree. put reason codes in responses so Console and SDKs can surface why a request was limited. e.g., `limited_by=reserved_capacity` or `limited_by=abuse_score_high`.

devon: rollback safety: we should support ephemeral override via feature flags and an emergency kill switch that treats QSvc responses as advisory (gateway ignores) for N minutes. also a canary rollout for QSvc where only 10% of orgs are on new policy.

infra-bot: deploy: quota-svc/v2 canary started on infra-canary-3 at 1832459800.helm: applied.

sam: doc and tests: we need contract tests for QSvc <-> gateway (latency, error semantics), and chaos tests for QSvc timeouts so gateways exercise fallback. also add synthetic traffic for abuse detection evaluation.

katie: action items: (1) I will open an RFC PR that describes interface (lease + acquire + score + reason codes) and region sharding model, (2) devon please draft contract tests, (3) miguel/anya please outline multi-region failover semantics, (4) sam add metrics dashboard mockups. I'll link the canary logs here once CI finishes.

devon: ack. I'll also add a feature-flag path and emergency-ignore toggle for initial rollout.

katie: thanks everyone. @infra-bot paste canary link when logs are up :thumbsup:
